description: The article operationalises clinical performance determinants through a longitudinal measurement burst design combining short-intensive weekly surveys with long-term tracking across placements.
title: Measurement burst design with multilevel location-scale structural equation modelling

description: The article defines an organizing distinction for intervention research: a mediator explains how or why a treatment works, while a moderator reflects who benefits.
title: Mediator–moderator distinction in randomized intervention research

description: The MeDOL framework is the review's organizing scheme, adapting Morrison et al.'s instructional effectiveness model to the diversity of LTA research.
title: MeDOL framework for reviewing learning-to-argue instructional approaches

description: The study's model of productive collaboration is the rating schema by Meier et al.
title: Meier et al. rating schema for productive collaboration

description: A taxonomy for coding think-aloud protocols of secondary school students studying a history text, developed by Meijer et al.
title: Meijer et al. taxonomy of 56 metacognitive text-studying activities

description: The author argues that comparing feeble-minded children with normal children of the same chronological age reveals only differences attributable to developmental level, not to feeble-mindedness itself.
title: Mental-age-matched comparison method

description: The article details procedures for reducing heterogeneous survey data to the common basis of mental age.
title: Mental-age score conversion and norming method

description: The review applies a scoring tool based on the five sources of validity originally described by Messick: content, response process, internal structure, relation to other variables, and consequences.
title: Messick's five-source validity framework for surgical assessment tools

description: The article anchors its validity discussion in Messick's unified theory of validity, which holds that validity is a property of inferences and decisions based on scores, not of instruments.
title: Messick's six-source unified validity framework for AI evaluation

description: The commentary grounds its critique in Messick's unified validity framework, which \"conceptualizes validity as integrated sources of evidence encompassing construct representation, sources of construct-irrelevant variance and the social consequences of score use.\" Within this framework, speededness
title: Messick's unified validity framework for assessment

description: Meta-d' is a signal detection theoretic measure of relative metacognitive accuracy, attributed in the article to Maniscalco and Lau (2012), that explicitly models the relation between primary task performance and metacognition.
title: Meta-d′ as a performance-normalized measure of metacognitive efficiency

description: The article uses a review-of-reviews design: comprehensive multi-database searching identified 29 systematic reviews of digital asthma self-management interventions, which were then quality-appraised with AMSTAR so that only reviews meeting predetermined standards (at least 50% of quality indicators
title: Metareview method: systematic review of systematic reviews with AMSTAR quality filtering

description: The review organises the design of intensive longitudinal studies around core methodological parameters: study duration, assessment frequency, sampling scheme (fixed, random, semi-random, event-based), item phrasing and questionnaire density, and data-collection device.
title: Methodological parameter framework for designing intensive longitudinal studies

description: The article introduces a framework targeted at facilitating the reproducibility of meta-analysis, organized in four levels building on the TOP-guidelines, the Reproducibility Enhancement Principles, and Lakens et al.'s recommendations.
title: Methods Reproducibility framework for meta-analysis: four levels from Computational Reproducibility to Outcome Reproducibility

description: The article organizes experimental work on geometry teaching around three questions: whether the desired results are obtained under a given method, what the best method of obtaining them is, and whether obtaining them transfers to other subjects.
title: Metzler's three lines of experimental investigation for geometry pedagogy
